questions.question: Will the RTO-wide clearing price in PJM Interconnection's capacity auction for delivery year 2025/2026 be above $100 per MW-day?
questions.value: $269.92 per MW-day, against $28.92 in the previous auction
questions.source: PJM Interconnection, press release on the 2025/2026 Base Residual Auction, 30 July 2024
questions.note: More than ninefold in one auction.

questions.question: Will PJM's capacity auction for delivery year 2026/2027 clear at its new FERC-approved price cap across the whole footprint?
questions.value: $329.17 per MW-day, the cap, for the entire PJM footprint
questions.source: PJM Interconnection, press release on the 2026/2027 Base Residual Auction, 22 July 2025
questions.note: The cap and a floor were new rules for this auction; clearing at the cap means the market wanted to pay more than the rules allowed.

questions.question: Will the average US retail price of electricity, all sectors, be more than 3% higher in 2024 than in 2023, according to the EIA?
questions.source: US Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Annual, Table 2.4
questions.note: Capacity prices jumped in PJM while the national retail average rose about 2%.

questions.question: Will the IEA estimate that data centres worldwide used more than 400 TWh of electricity in 2024?
questions.value: 415 TWh, about 1.5% of world electricity use
questions.source: International Energy Agency, Energy and AI, executive summary, April 2025
questions.note: April 2025 vintage. A later IEA publication gives 485 TWh for 2025.

questions.question: Will Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's December 2024 report put US data centres above 4% of total US electricity use in 2023?
questions.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report, December 2024
questions.note: December 2024 vintage. LBNL's June 2026 update estimates 4.7% for 2024 and revises earlier years slightly downward.

questions.question: Will LBNL's next Queued Up report show less capacity waiting for US grid interconnection at the end of 2024 than the roughly 2,600 GW at the end of 2023?
questions.value: About 2,290 GW at end-2024 (1,400 GW generation, 890 GW storage)
questions.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Queued Up: 2025 Edition, December 2025
questions.note: More than 700 GW withdrew in 2024 while about 500 GW of new requests arrived.

questions.question: Will more than 12 GW of utility-scale battery storage be added to the US grid in 2024, according to the EIA?
questions.source: US Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 12 March 2025
questions.note: Developers had planned 14.3 GW for 2024: plans ran well ahead of what was built.

questions.question: Will worldwide semiconductor sales for 2024, as reported by the SIA from WSTS data, exceed $600 billion?
questions.source: Semiconductor Industry Association, press release, 7 February 2025
questions.note: WSTS had forecast $588 billion in November 2023 and later revised the 2024 total to $630.5 billion.

questions.question: Will the International Federation of Robotics report more than 550,000 industrial robots installed worldwide in 2023?
questions.source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2024 press release, 24 September 2024
questions.note: The second-highest year on record, but below 2022.

questions.question: In the IFR's World Robotics data, will China account for more than half of worldwide industrial robot installations in 2024?
questions.source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2025 press release, 25 September 2025

questions.question: Will the June 2025 TOP500 list include more than three systems above 1 exaflop/s on the HPL benchmark?
questions.value: Three: El Capitan (1.742), Frontier (1.353) and Aurora (1.012 exaflop/s)
questions.note: A fourth system reached exactly 1.000 exaflop/s on the November 2025 list.

questions.question: In McLean and Pontiff's study of published stock-return predictors, will portfolio returns be more than 50% lower after publication than in the original samples?
questions.value: 58% lower after publication; 26% lower out of sample
questions.source: R. D. McLean and J. Pontiff, Journal of Finance 71(1), 2016
questions.note: Mainländer's voice in data: an edge begins to die the moment it is published.

questions.question: In Hou, Xue and Zhang's replication of 452 anomalies, with microcaps controlled, will more than half fail to clear |t| ≥ 1.96?
questions.source: K. Hou, C. Xue and L. Zhang, Replicating Anomalies, Review of Financial Studies 33(5), 2020
questions.note: Precise and wrong: most published results did not survive a careful re-run.

questions.question: Under their Bayesian model, will more than 75% of the US factors in Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen's study replicate?
questions.value: 82.4% (55.6% with plain OLS tests on raw returns)
questions.source: T. I. Jensen, B. Kelly and L. H. Pedersen, Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?, Journal of Finance 78(5), 2023
questions.note: The same evidence reads as crisis or as robustness depending on the method — which is why the method is published before the score.
